resolvedQuestions.answer: A constant second directive under Directives:, dedup-bounded (~0 suppressed, ~150-250 chars per delivery episode), never self-silent; fails the 022 bar on both prongs — refuse.

Measured live: (a) portable via shared renderer; (b) indexes shared rules in siblings through the linked .skilled dir but misses sibling-local rules at root repo-rules/ (out-of-root symlink skip); (c) weakest via per-runtime invisibility traps.

resolvedQuestions.answer: No new model-facing surface: the coverage is a designed partition (Gate 5 + AGENTS.md §8 loader + resident floor). The real fragility is CI-side — no check that trigger rows cover rule fires.

Repo rules reach the model only via Gate 5 at the first write, action-matched through REPO RULES.md; read-only turns never fire it, and AGENTS.md §8 separately loads the five reply-fired rules by name on every substantive reply.
Rule rows in Gate 1 lookup output, self-silent on vocabulary miss but firing on read-only turns; <1% artifact growth; reverses retrieval-conventions.md:284 and misses sibling-local rules — refuse.

Weak form (per-action classification) refused: <=4/13 rules tool-observable, riskiest commands already guarded. Strong form (once-per-session first-mutation reminder via the Gate-3 marker pattern) is the single admissible build, gated on a measured miss or operator risk acceptance.

keyFindings.title: **022 bar test.** The hygiene directive survives the bar because it "names a specific prohibition a pre-commit gate enforces" [SOURCE: injection-contract.md:52-54; render.ts:110-112]. A Gate-5 pointer restates `AGENTS.md:93-101` — content the always-loaded document already carries verbatim — and no mechanical gate enforces the trigger-table load (no hook denies a write that skipped it). It fails the bar's duplication prong unless framed for runtimes where `AGENTS.md` is absent — the exact reason hygiene exists [SOURCE: render.ts:110-112] — and even then it lacks the enforcement prong.

keyFindings.title: **But the tool-observable action space covers a minority of the corpus.** Mapping all 13 rules' fire lists: tool-visible triggers exist for `blast-radius` (rm/git/npm/curl commands), `skill-hub-routing` (registry/graph path prefixes), `prevent-overengineering` (new-file Write, weakly), `scope-discipline` (out-of-scope paths — needs frozen scope a hook cannot see). The other 9 — uncertainty, evidence, answer-the-actual-request, communication×4, delegation, root-cause (retry detection needs history) — fire inside reasoning or prose with no tool call to key on [SOURCE: REPO RULES.md:40-52 fire lists]. A PreToolUse advisory is structurally blind to the majority of the corpus.

keyFindings.title: **Emission shape.** `renderAdvisorBrief` emits `Advisor: {live|stale}; use {skill} {conf}/{unc} pass.` (route block), then unconditionally appends `DIRECTIVES_LABEL` + `HYGIENE_DIRECTIVE` [SOURCE: render.ts:438-449]. A repo-rules pointer would be a second constant directive under `Directives:`, registered as a new policy id — `directiveBlockIds()` currently carries only `POLICY_COMMENT_HYGIENE_ID` [SOURCE: render.ts:102-106]. It would also ride the three fallback heads (`outage`, `skipped`, `no-match`), which append the same directive block [SOURCE: render.ts:476-489]. Emitted text ≈ one additional ~120–200-char line.

keyFindings.title: **Gate 5 under federation.** Works by contract, not mechanism: the sibling's `AGENTS.md` is the same file (symlink), its `REPO RULES.md` is its own real table routing to its own `repo-rules/` — the design keeps the corpus federated while the router stays local [SOURCE: `ls -la "Obsidian Plugin/"`]. This is why the corpus-rooted surfaces are the wrong layer: the *routing* is deliberately per-repo even where the *content* is shared.

keyFindings.title: **Match key: none — constant.** It cannot condition on action or topic; it appears on every delivered brief including pure-read turns, so it fires precisely where Gate 5 deliberately does not.

A rule surfaced because the prompt *mentions* rollbacks arrives on turns where the model takes no mutating action at all.

keyFindings.title: **Per-turn cost.** Marginal: 13 docs × ~17–30 phrases ≈ +~300 phrases onto a committed artifact that already holds 33,688 phrases across 3.7 MB — under 1% growth; parse cost per lookup is unchanged in shape (the artifact is parsed cold each call) [SOURCE: trigger-index.json measured; lookup-trigger-index.mjs:77-93]. The real cost is a row added to Gate 1's surfaced context whenever phrases match — a suggestion the model may then spend a Read on.

keyFindings.title: **Portability trap shared by (b) and any corpus-level surface.** The walker dedupes by resolved path and refuses a symlink whose target lands outside the repo root: `'symlink target outside the repository'` [SOURCE: corpus.mjs:299-310,334-342]. In sibling repos the shared rule files are symlinks INTO this checkout [SOURCE: specs/agents/010-repo-rule-system-integration/research/synthesis.md:13,31] — so an index built in a sibling would either skip them as out-of-root links or index duplicates, and `corpusRootsFor` only rewrites the `.skilled/` spelling anyway [SOURCE: corpus.mjs:44-51]. The federation shape works against a corpus-rooted surface.

keyFindings.title: **Silence condition: none of its own.** The directive is constant; it has no condition beyond the brief itself. Its delivery is governed by the lifecycle dedup, not by relevance: full delivery on first proven message, every lifecycle boundary, directives-payload change, transcript reset, or any fail-open doubt [SOURCE: directive-lifecycle.ts:139-153,165-178]. On suppressed turns the model gets only `parts.head` (the Advisor line, ~43 bytes: `ROUTE_ONLY_ESTIMATED_BYTES`) [SOURCE: render.ts:99; directive-lifecycle.ts:149,179].

A "suggest rules" variant of (a) means admitting rules into the advisor's scored corpus — a topic-matched recommendation polluting the skill-routing contract, symmetric to the REPO RULES.md §4 carve-out ("Out: skill routing" — the layers are deliberately separate) [SOURCE: scorer/types.ts:47; REPO RULES.md:90-94].

Its `REPO RULES.md` is a distinct real file (9,581 bytes) with its own trigger table [SOURCE: `ls -la "Obsidian Plugin/"`].

keyFindings.title: **The federation is real and changes the portability calculus.** Nine-plus rule files are symlinked into sibling repos (`Mobile CLI`, `Obsidian Plugin`) whose `AGENTS.md` files are absolute symlinks into this checkout; the shared corpus is one physical file set reached from multiple roots [SOURCE: specs/agents/010-repo-rule-system-integration/research/synthesis.md:13,31]. In this checkout the 13 files are real files, not links (verified `ls -la`). Any new surface keyed on `.skilled/repo-rules/` must resolve correctly where the directory itself is a federation mount.

keyFindings.title: **The genuinely uncovered cell is narrow.** Of 13 rules: 5 are reply-fired (§8 loader), 8 are action-fired (Gate 5). Of the 8, four — uncertainty, evidence, root-cause, delegation — can also fire on pure read-only reasoning turns (diagnose, answer-without-certainty, judge a delegation), where neither loader reaches them. What is uncovered there is only the rules' *expanded* text; their binding clauses are the resident floor (precedence level 3, REPO RULES.md:22-27).

keyFindings.title: **The injection channel inventory is mapped, and it contains a portability trap.** The advisor brief is `[SYS]` model-context-only on Claude/Cursor/Devin/Codex/OpenCode and `[MSG]` visible on Pi [SOURCE: injection-contract.md:50-68]. Tool-time hooks exist and are the candidate (c) precedent: dispatch-preflight-lint `[BLOCK]`/`[SYS]` [SOURCE: injection-contract.md:155-164], mcp-route-guard `[SYS]` except OpenCode where it is `[LOG]`-only — "genuinely invisible to the OpenCode model" [SOURCE: injection-contract.md:166-172]. Post-edit-quality on Claude Code and Devin writes plain stdout that "likely never reach[es] the assistant's context at all in normal use" — confirmed for Claude, unverified for Devin [SOURCE: injection-contract.md:201].

keyFindings.title: **The once-per-session mechanism is directly cloneable.** Gate 3 delivers `GATE_3_MUTATION_NOTICE` once at the first non-exempt mutation via a persisted session marker (`gate3DeliveryMarker`, `recordGate3NoticeDelivered`); "an open gate speaks once … a mutation after that delivery stays silent" [SOURCE: spec-gate-core.mjs:1736-1783,376-444]. A "first write → remember Gate 5" advisory is the same shape: one `additionalContext` line per session at first mutation.

keyFindings.title: **The only admissible form that survives all four tests** is the strong-form (c): a once-per-session `additionalContext` at the first non-exempt mutation — "match your action against `REPO RULES.md` and load every firing rule." It names a declared [HARD] BLOCK at the moment it binds (022 bar ✓), matches the action event not the topic (table semantics ✓), self-silences via the cloneable Gate-3 marker (cost ≈ ~1 line/session, measured precedent ~1–33 advises/day) (✓), and needs a per-runtime adapter (portability △). **Its blocker: no measured Gate-5 miss rate exists**, so admission today would be speculative — it is a candidate for build only if a miss is observed or the operator accepts the unmeasured risk [SOURCE: decisions.md:33-36; cross-lineage-synthesis.md:81].

keyFindings.title: **The read-only-turn gap is mostly covered by the promotion pattern.** Rules binding on read turns (uncertainty, evidence, communication, answering) already have their load-bearing clauses promoted into the always-loaded `AGENTS.md` §3–§4 — Confidence Thresholds, Restraint Signals, Verification Standards, Communication sections. This is the remedy 022 itself prescribed: "a clause that must bind while reading belongs where it always loads … promotion into the resident layer, not injection" [SOURCE: 001-deep-research/implementation-summary.md:55].

No measured miss rate exists — and per the 022 rule, an unmeasured rate cannot justify a surface [SOURCE: decisions.md:33-36].

keyFindings.statement: The advisor brief fires every user prompt; the constant directive is deduped via directive-lifecycle.ts.
Blast radius: render.ts three emit sites + OpenCode plugin mirror + exact-string tests.
All candidates respect 010's no-rule-growth constraint; emitted text must never embed the corpus path.
010's constraint: content that must bind while reading cannot live in a rule file; the rule set should not grow.
022's measurement lesson: event frequency must be read from the log, never reasoned about.
Candidate (a) fails 022's bar: restates a Gate-5 disposition, names no gate-enforced prohibition; hygiene asymmetry.
022's admission bar refuses prompt-time injections that restate a disposition; only a gate-enforced prohibition earns a slot.
A static second load path already exists where Gate 5 cannot reach replies (AGENTS.md:261).
Gate 5 fires on the first write of a session only; read-only turns never fire it.
Candidate (d): no measured miss exists; flip test = measured miss with cost; status quo covers first-write and replies.
The router matches on the action about to be taken, never the prompt topic.
Candidate (c) matches on action — the router's own key; only candidate addressing later-in-session actions; shared core + per-runtime wiring.
Candidate (b) matches prompt topic, never action; trigger-table action phrases absent from rule trigger_phrases; complementary to Gate 5.
No tool-call-to-trigger-row mapping module exists today; spec-gate classifies spec-folder intent, not rule rows.
Portability: canonical .skilled path wins dedupe; sibling reads shared index via .skilled symlink; root 'repo-rules' breaks sibling; one static root cannot serve both layouts.
Candidate (b) is one line at corpus.mjs:30; generator indexes 13 docs / 255 phrases; 7 single-token phrases never rank.
Dedup: full on first/boundaries/content-change/transcript-shrink; route-only on proven repeats; fail-safe full otherwise.
Federation: canonical corpus .skilled/repo-rules (13 files); Public/repo-rules is a symlink layer; Obsidian holds 12 of 13 symlinked; answer-the-actual-request.md never propagated.
Maintenance: staleness is phrase-set only; publication fail-closed corpus-wide; corpus checker internal-only.
Candidate (c) silence: no row match + once-per-session dedup with re-arm; cost: process spawn per matched event + ~100-200B advisory; frequency log-measured post-build.
Pointer text must name the repo-root router, never the corpus path.
Cross-candidate: only (c) action-keyed; (a) fails 022 bar; (b) reverses documented decision, topic-keyed; (d) no measured miss/win; (c) strongest precedent, open risk classifier quality.

Empirical: today rule-vocab prompts return 0 results exit 1; simulated hits are 0.880 query-containment ('add a retry'->root-cause, 'force push'->blast-radius, 'unsolicited warning'->answer-the-actual-request).
Silence: scoring-only drops score-0 rows and exits 1; 2 of 5 realistic prompts zero-hit.
Rule phrase 'silent reinterpretation' is already an index key owned by another document; index tolerates multi-owner phrases; corpus collision hygiene is index-blind.
Corpus is 13 rule files with 255 trigger_phrases total; phrases name dispositions, not tool actions.
Measured sizes: route 42B, label 12B, hygiene 207B, full brief ~261B; pointer draft 162B (~40 tokens).
Candidate (a) is a prompt-time reminder surface, not action-keyed; value is timing and AGENTS.md-absent runtimes.
No repo-relevance signal in the renderer; handler carries workspaceRoot; unconditional emission fires in repos without REPO RULES.md.
Brief emission: three emit sites (render.ts:441,449,486); route capped at 80 tokens; directives appended after cap.
Documented decision-against at retrieval-conventions.md:284 states the structural reason; admission must overturn it explicitly.
The trigger index deliberately excludes .skilled/repo-rules; the documented reason is that indexing them would surface a rule as a context candidate.
Candidate (c) shape: advisory naming rule file(s) for the matched action; spec-gate precedent proves delivery machinery; tool-call→row mapping does not exist today.
Index: 3,738,528 bytes / 33,688 phrases / 13,172 paths; growth +13 paths, +255 phrases, est. +10-25KB; parse dominates per-lookup.
